A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ComGS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated limitations and renumbered results.

before.justification: v1 reports original ComGS reconstruction results on N3DV and MeetRoom, component ablations, hyperparameter studies, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds perceptual metrics, long-video reconstruction results, and an evaluated random-access variant.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a random-access variant: non-key frames reference the preceding key frame, key frames reference earlier key frames, and periodic I-frames interrupt dependencies. This is a limited procedural adaptation; the original keypoint selection, motion propagation, and correction framework remains.

E1.justification: The same N3DV and MeetRoom datasets and indoor reconstruction domains remain. v2 additionally evaluates reconstruction configured for random access on N3DV, introducing a playback requirement beyond sequential streaming. The longer Flame Salmon sequence retains the existing scene and domain.

E2.justification: QUEEN-s is added to the MeetRoom comparison in Table 1. E-NeRF and TGH appear in the new long-video comparison alongside 4DGS, which was already evaluated in v1's appendix. Table 1's 4DGS-to-4D-GS rename preserves the same cited baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds SSIM and LPIPS to the main evaluation, a 1,200-frame Flame Salmon experiment, and evaluation of the random-access configuration. The original experiments retain their stated camera splits, preprocessing, training budgets, and key-frame intervals.

E4.justification: The component, neighboring-point control, error-awareness, keypoint-count, GoF, and correction-weight ablations retain identical results. The motion and error visual analyses also remain. The new long-video and random-access tables report additional performance evaluations rather than extending these diagnostic analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical significance reporting without changing that practice.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are retained, but reported outcomes expand substantially through SSIM/LPIPS scores, the MeetRoom QUEEN-s row, and two new evaluations. Table 2 reports long-video ComGS-s results of 29.56 dB and 0.053 MB; Table 6 adds reconstruction-quality and storage results for random access across six scenes.

T1.justification: The added standard covariance-projection equation in Section 3.1 and revised indexing and set notation clarify existing 3DGS operations. They introduce no substantive new mathematical argument, formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: motion-sensitive keypoints, adaptive motion propagation, and error-aware correction. The headline 159-fold and 14-fold storage reductions and competitive fidelity/rendering claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 newly explains previous-frame dependence as a restriction on random access and describes how the adaptation addresses it. The initialization, dense-view-input, and training-time limitations were already in v1 Appendix C and are relocated to v2's conclusion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address, explicitly documents the standard sequences' 300-frame length, and provides random-access implementation guidance, including an example 60-frame I-frame interval. Existing hyperparameters and compression details remain. The checklist still promises future code release, so actual availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused Gaussian-compression related-work subsection and references covering contextual coding, TGH, FreeTimeGS, and E-NeRF. The Neural Scene Flow Fields reference disappears. These additions broaden context while preserving the central positioning around motion sharing for compact online reconstruction.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization remain. v2 clarifies notation, key-frame reconstruction, and ablation descriptions; moves limitations into the conclusion; and adds related-work and random-access subsections, acknowledgements, and the NeurIPS checklist. These are localized expansions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains metric columns and a comparator row, and two tables are added for long-video and random-access results. Existing tables and figures are repositioned, with minor label and formatting corrections. All nine figures and the original result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The perceptual metrics, long-video comparison, and evaluated random-access adaptation broaden support for the paper's quality and practical-applicability claims while preserving the original evidence. The gains are useful but limited: random-access evaluation reports quality and storage without access latency, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
